comparison: Both evaluate the PTZ-induced seizure susceptibility finding (C5, C106). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes an apparent contradiction with prior literature (C4) requiring further investigation. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding as 'convincing' without raising concerns about the contradiction.

Both evaluate the comprehensive electrophysiological characterization (C8-C16). OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers explicitly noting improved statistical analysis and increased sample sizes. Complete agreement on the evidence for decreased eIPSC, unchanged eEPSC, increased E/I ratio, and postsynaptic mechanism.

Perfect overlap on immunofluorescence data showing reduced inhibitory markers (C17-C25). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'substantial quantity of data' and developmental time course analysis, fully aligning with OpenEval's assessment.

Complete agreement on surface GABAAR reduction findings (C26-C33). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of immunofluorescence and biotinylation approaches, while peer reviewers note the authors 'addressed the concerns adequately' regarding these data.

Both evaluate super-resolution microscopy data (C34-C40) showing EndoA1 colocalization with inhibitory markers. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on convergence with biochemical data (C43-C46). Peer reviewers accept the imaging data as part of the 'broad array of experimental approaches' without specific critique.

Both address biochemical interaction data (C43-C46). OpenEval includes these claims with super-resolution data in R4, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers separately affirm the co-IP experiments demonstrating EndoA1-gephyrin-GABAAR complexes. Complete agreement on the evidence.

Both evaluate the EndoA1-gephyrin interaction discovery (C47-C51, C103). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED emphasizing multiple validation approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly state this is 'a novel component...providing a valuable addition to the field' and affirm the specificity for A1 over A2/A3.

Both address gephyrin clustering and rescue experiments (C52-C60). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing functional consequences and rescue specificity. Peer reviewers accept the clustering data and subdomain identification without challenge. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate GABAAR localization to gephyrin puncta (C63-C65). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic details remain incompletely resolved. Peer reviewers affirm the finding as demonstrating EndoA1 'promotes assembly of the inhibitory postsynaptic element' without expressing concerns about mechanistic gaps.

Both address domain mapping experiments (C66-C71). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting all domains are required. Peer reviewers explicitly mention 'identifying the subdomains of Endophilin A1 that contribute to this effect,' indicating acceptance of the structure-function analysis.

Perfect overlap on actin depolymerization experiments (C74-C83). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the temporal sequence showing gephyrin loss precedes GABAAR loss. Peer reviewers accept these pharmacological manipulations as part of the comprehensive experimental approach.

Both evaluate epistasis analysis with p140Cap (C85-C90). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on genetic interaction experiments. Peer reviewers accept the pathway relationship without challenge, implicitly affirming the logic of the rescue experiments.

Both address mutant rescue experiments (C91-C94). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, demonstrating requirement for both membrane binding and p140Cap interaction. Peer reviewers affirm the dual functionality findings, noting the authors demonstrate 'underlying mechanisms' through subdomain analysis.

Both evaluate in vivo AAV rescue experiments (C95-C97). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing convergence of behavioral, electrophysiological, and molecular data. Peer reviewers explicitly support the rescue data demonstrating functional significance. Complete agreement.

Both address the overarching conclusions (C98-C99, C104-C105). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on data convergence. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm EndoA1 as 'a novel regulator of GABAergic synapses' and describe findings as 'valuable.' Complete agreement on the main conclusions.

Both evaluate broad spatial distribution and non-redundant function (C109-C110, C114-C115, C117, C103-C106). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting the distinct mechanism. Peer reviewers accept the comprehensive subcellular analysis and specificity for A1, affirming the novelty of the findings.

Both address the proposed mechanistic model (C122, C134). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting these are speculative proposals lacking direct evidence. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the model as consistent with experimental findings without challenging its speculative nature. Divergence in evaluation stringency.

Both address background literature on iPSD organization mechanisms (C100-C101, C118-C121). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting accurate citations and appropriate context. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these contextual claims without challenge. Agreement on the appropriateness of background framing.

Both address speculative claims (C107-C108, C140-C142, C102, C116, C139). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting C142 and C139 lack direct experimental support. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriately framed discussion points. Divergence reflects different standards for speculative content.

Both evaluate extensive background literature citations (C123-C133 and others). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting accurate citations providing mechanistic context. Peer reviewers implicitly accept all background claims without challenge. Complete agreement on the appropriateness of literature context.

Both address speculative hypothesis about p140Cap coordination (C138-C139). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting C139 is 'pure speculation without experimental support.' Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED as an appropriate future direction. Divergence in evaluation of unsupported hypotheses.

Both evaluate established background knowledge from prior literature (C1-C4, C6-C7, C41-C42, C61-C62, C72-C73, C76, C84, C111-C113, C135-C138, C140-C141). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting accurate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept all contextual claims. Complete agreement.

Both address F-actin distribution observation (C73). OpenEval includes this with other background literature as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers separately note this as a supporting observation accepted without challenge. Agreement on this contextual finding.

OpenEval evaluates functional specialization versus redundancy claims (C6-C7, C111-C113, C116, C135-C137) as SUPPORTED, noting the molecular basis for specificity remains unclear. Peer reviewers include these in general background acceptance. Agreement on the evidence but OpenEval more explicit about knowledge gaps.
